w:r.w:t: For Projects Selected for the Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund (AEIF)

This AEIF Branding & Communications Guideline sets out the visual identity and messaging standards for all projects selected to receive funding from the Alumni Engagement Innovation Fund (AEIF) of the U.S. Department of State.
The goals of this guideline are to:
Ensure that U.S. Government support is clearly and correctly acknowledged in all AEIF-funded activities and materials.
Promote a coherent and professional visual identity that aligns with the Department of State’s Brand Policy and Brand System.
Ensure consistent use of Exchange Alumni (ExchangeAlumni) brand asset
Help alumni teams apply best practices in storytelling, photography, video, and social media.
This guideline applies only to AEIF-funded projects. Other alumni or Embassy programs may follow additional or different branding rules as provided by the U.S. Embassy or the Department of State.
All AEIF-funded projects are part of the public diplomacy work of the U.S. Department of State. As such, they must follow the Department’s official Brand Policy (10 FAM 413 & 415).
The standard, rectangular U.S. flag is the primary visual symbol indicating U.S. Government support.
The flag must appear on all public-facing materials linked to AEIF-funded activities, including but not limited to:
Social media graphics and digital posts
Flyers, posters, banners, and pull-up stands
The flag must always be displayed in absolute horizontal or absolute vertical orientation.
In any orientation, the union (blue field with stars) must be at the top left.
The proportions of the flag cannot be altered. Do not stretch it horizontally or vertically; always resize with aspect ratio locked.
The flag must appear in its official colors.
Recoloring the flag (e.g., making it monochrome, applying filters, or changing shades) is not permitted.
The flag may not be placed over or under other images, text, or artwork in a way that obscures it or changes its shape.
Abstract, wavy, or stylized versions of the flag are not allowed.
Always keep a clear “buffer” around the flag. The minimum clear space should be equal to the height of three flag stripes (the “x-height”) on all sides.
The flag must not touch other logos, seals, text, or the edge of the layout.
The Department of State (DOS) seal is a formal symbol of the U.S. Government.
It must appear in its upright orientation: the eagle facing left toward the olive branch, not rotated or flipped.
The seal must be shown in its full circular shape; do not crop it into other shapes.
Recoloring or changing the opacity of the seal is not permitted.
The seal may not be merged or combined with other artwork to create a new logo.
The seal is strongly recommended for:
Formal printed materials (programs, plaques, official invitations)

All social media posts about AEIF-funded activities should:
Tag relevant accounts (as appropriate to platform):
Focus on achievements, lessons learned, and community impact.
Obtain necessary consents for photos/videos, especially for minors.
Avoid partisan, inflammatory, or sensitive political statements.
Aim for images that are positive, inspiring, and authentic.
Prefer full-color images; you may convert to black-and-white later if needed.
Ensure subjects are in focus and well lit; avoid distracting backgrounds.
Take a variety of shots: wide, medium, close-up; group and individual.

Minimize background noise and avoid filming against bright backlighting.
For interviews, prepare a short question set (name, role, project benefit, etc.).
Use royalty-free or properly licensed music and credit it when appropriate.

Q1. Can our project create its own logo?
Yes. Your project may use a unique logo as long as it does not imitate or
incorporate the U.S. flag, DOS seal, or ExchangeAlumni logo and does not look like an official U.S. Government mark.
Q2. Can partner organizations place their logo above the U.S. flag?
No. The U.S. flag must always appear first and most prominently among logos.
Q3. Can we recolor the ExchangeAlumni logo to match our project colors?
No. The ExchangeAlumni logo must always use its official color palette (
Q4. Can we design our own version of the AEIF logo?
No. Use AEIF as a funding reference, not as a standalone brand. Do not create new “AEIF logos.”
Q5. Who should we coordinate with about media coverage and branding questions?
Coordinate with your U.S. Embassy Public Affairs Section or the sponsoring Department of State office before issuing press releases, holding large public events, or producing branded merchandise.
